pages.text: "No greens!" Bung fished green leaves from the noodles onto the boat edge and pushed orange shrimp away. Their noodle boat floated still, tied to a post. Little Ddori ate green leaves happily.
"Mom, I will take bowls to the customers today!" Mom smiled and offered a bowl. Only white noodles remained in Bung's own bowl. Ddori pointed at the shrimp.
Next morning, smoke rose from the stove. Bung lifted a noodle bowl, arms shaking. "The bowl keeps tipping!"
Mom called Bung beside the stove. Green leaves, orange shrimp, and white noodles lay beside a big pot. "Wow..." Bung stretched to see.
Mom dropped in a handful of greens. The broth shimmered green. "All three colors make a bowl. Green gives your legs strength, orange your arms strength, white energy to play."
She served all three together. Green, orange, white steamed side by side. Mom tapped the bowl rim. "Greens and shrimp—slurp!"
Bung slurped a leaf. "Oh! Soft!" Crunch went a shrimp. Bung drew Ddori's hand close. "Greens and shrimp—slurp, Ddori!"
An empty bowl, and light-feeling arms! Bung lifted it high. A big boat rocked theirs, but the bowl stayed steady. Bung hopped.
Bung offered a noodle bowl straight toward a customer boat with both hands. "One, a green bite! Two, an orange bite! Three, a white bite!" A big hand reached to take it.
Mom touched her forehead to Bung's cheek. All three colors gave strength to hold bowls. Bung put shrimp on Ddori's noodles. "Greens and shrimp—slurp!"
